title: 1992 AMC 8 Problem 23
statement: If two dice are tossed, the probability that the product of the numbers showing on the tops of the dice is greater than \(10\) is

solutions.text:
There are \(36\) equally likely outcomes. Counting the ordered pairs whose product exceeds \(10\): with a first die of \(2\) there is \(1\) (namely \(2 \times 6\)); of \(3\), there are \(3\); of \(4\), there are \(4\); of \(5\), there are \(4\); of \(6\), there are \(5.\)

That is \(1 + 3 + 4 + 4 + 5 = 17\) favorable outcomes, so the probability is \(\dfrac{17}{36}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: There are \(6 \times 6 = 36\) equally likely outcomes; count those whose product exceeds \(10\)
Make a \(6 \times 6\) multiplication table and mark every product greater than \(10\)
